question: In covering a distance of 150 km, Pranay takes 2 hours more than Aman. If Pranay doubles his speed, then he would take 3 hours less than Aman. Pranay's speed is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Pranay's speed ratio (Original : New) = 1 : 2 ⇒ Time ratio = 2 : 1.

Difference in time ratio = 2 − 1 = 1 unit.

Actual time difference = (Aman's time + 2) − (Aman's time − 3) = 5 hours.

⇒ 1 unit = 5 hours ⇒ Original time = 10 hours ⇒ Speed = 150 ÷ 10 = 15 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 150 km

Pranay's original time = Aman's time + 2 hours

Pranay's time at double speed = Aman's time − 3 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

When Distance is constant, Speed ∝ 1 / Time

 
• 
 
 
 Start
 End
 Distance = 150 km
 
 Speed = P
 
 Time = t
 
 Speed = 2P
 
 Time = t − 5

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original time taken by Pranay be T hours.

⇒ When Pranay's speed is doubled, his time becomes half = T / 2 hours.

⇒ Difference in Pranay's time = T − T / 2 = T / 2 hours.

⇒ From the given conditions, the actual difference in his time is also the difference between his times relative to Aman.

⇒ Time difference = (Aman's time + 2) − (Aman's time − 3) = 5 hours.

⇒ Therefore, T / 2 = 5 ⇒ T = 10 hours.

⇒ Pranay's original speed = Distance ÷ T

⇒ Pranay's original speed = 150 ÷ 10 = 15 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality

When distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional. S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂.

Average Speed

If equal distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed is (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|. For opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
